questions.question: If a cylinder with radius (R) and Length (L) is given, give the expression to find out the twisting couple of the cylinder
questions.solution_html:
• If a cylinder with radius (R) and length (L) is given, give the expression to find out
  • the twisting couple of the cylinder.
  • Answer
  • Twisting couple, C = (π η R⁴ θ) (2L). ((1 mark))
  • η – rigidity modulus, R – radius, L – length, θ – angle of twist. ((1 mark))

questions.question: Explain about the different elastic behavior of solids.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  • Solids obey Hooke’s law for small deformations. ((1 mark))
  • Beyond the elastic limit, permanent deformation starts. ((1 mark))
  • Ductile materials show large plastic strain before breaking. ((1 mark))
  • Brittle materials break without much deformation. ((1 mark))
  • Area under stress–strain curve shows resilience and toughness. ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Area under stress–strain curve shows resilience and toughness. ()
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How can we compare moments of inertia using torsion pendulum?
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  • Time period T = 2π√(I/C). ((1 mark))
  • Measure time period of platform alone (T₀) and with the body (T). ((1 mark))
  • Moment of inertia of body, I = (C/4π²)(T² – T₀²). ((1 mark))
  • For two bodies, I₁/I₂ = (T₁² – T₀²)/(T₂² – T₀²). ((1 mark))
  • Hence moments of inertia can be compared experimentally. ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Option (c) . ((1 mark))

questions.question: Draw and explain the stress strain diagram.
questions.solution_html:
• Draw and explain the stress–strain diagram.
  • Answer
  • In the beginning, stress is directly proportional to strain (Hooke’s law). ((1 mark))
  • Elastic limit is the point up to which the body regains its shape. ((1 mark))
  • Beyond yield point, plastic deformation begins. ((1 mark))
  • Maximum stress is the ultimate strength; then necking and fracture occur. ((1 mark))
  • Curve differs for ductile and brittle materials. ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Curve differs for ductile and brittle materials. ()

questions.question: Explain the molecular theory of surface tension.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  • Molecules inside the liquid attract equally in all directions. ((1 mark))
  • Surface molecules have a net inward force. ((1 mark))
  • Surface acts like a stretched elastic membrane. ((1 mark))
  • Surface tension is the force per unit length. ((1 mark))
  • It causes spherical drops and capillary rise. ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: It causes spherical drops and capillary rise. ()

questions.question: Calculate the Reynold’s number for water flowing through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m at avelocity 2 m/s. Given density of water=1000 kg/m3 and viscosity of water=0.001 Pa.s
questions.solution_html:
• Calculate the Reynold’s number for water flowing through a pipe of diameter 0.1 m
  • at a velocity 2 m/s. Given density = 1000 kg/m³ and viscosity = 0.001 Pa·s.
  • Answer
  • Formula: Re = (ρ v D) / μ. ((1 mark))
  • Substitute: Re = (1000 × 2 × 0.1) 0.001. ((1 mark))
  • Re = 2 × 10⁵. ((1 mark))
  • Re > 4000, so the flow is turbulent. ((1 mark))
  • Reynolds number is dimensionless. ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Option (d) / μ. ((1 mark))

questions.question: How is ultrasonic is used in flaw detection?
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  • Ultrasonic waves reflect from cracks or defects in metals. ((1 mark))
  • A pulse is sent and reflected echoes are received. ((1 mark))
  • Time of echo gives the position of the flaw. ((1 mark))
  • No echo indicates a good region. ((1 mark))
  • Used for non-destructive testing in industries. ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Used for non-destructive testing in industries. ()

questions.question: Calculate the velocity with which a source of frequency 10000 Hz should approach an observer at rest in order to produce a Doppler shift of 200 Hz. Velocity of sound 332m/s.
questions.solution_html:
• Calculate the velocity with which a source of frequency 10000 Hz should approach
  • an observer at rest in order to produce a Doppler shift of 200 Hz. Velocity of sound =
  • 332 m/s.
  • Answer
  • Given f = 10000 Hz, f′ = 10200 Hz, v = 332 m/s. ((1 mark))
  • Formula: f′ = f ×. ((1 mark))
  • 10200/10000 = 332 (332 – vₛ). ((1 mark))
  • vₛ = 6.5 m/s. ((1 mark))
  • Hence, the source must approach at about 6.5 m/s. ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Hence, the source must approach at about 6.5 m/s. ()
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the significance of Mach number in classifying the motion of an aircraft.
questions.solution_html:
• Answer
  • Mach number M = V a (speed speed of sound). ((1 mark))
  • M < 1: subsonic, M = 1: sonic, M > 1: supersonic. ((1 mark))
  • Compressibility effects increase with M. ((1 mark))
  • Shock waves form when M ≥ 1. ((1 mark))
  • Mach number helps classify aircraft speed and design. ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: Mach number helps classify aircraft speed and design. ()
